titolo: GitHub skill lifts local LLM serving speed on GPUs and quantizations
descr: The new inference‑optimisation skill automates performance tuning and shows notable token‑per‑second gains on Intel and NVIDIA hardware.
paragrafi: The repository sybil-solutions/inference-optimisation-skill appeared in GitHub trending on 2026-11-16.

The skill first computes a theoretical ceiling, then adjusts one lever at a time, measures against interleaved controls, and logs every result. It only publishes a build that passes six acceptance gates and a long‑context stability check.

On an Intel Arc B390 iGPU the Ornith‑1.5‑35B‑A3B model improved decode from 43.6 to 53 tok/s for one user and from 84.7 to 103 tok/s for four users. Prefill at 32 K rose from 1,037 to 1,660 tok/s, and at 256 K from 297 to 628 tok/s (2.1×). Startup time fell from 113 to 43 seconds.

An Intel Arc Pro B70 running Qwen3.8‑27B reached 91.2 tok/s for a single user and 365 tok/s for sixteen users with EXL3 and custom XPU kernels. The same card with llama.cpp Q4_K_M recorded 25.0 tok/s decode. RTX 3090 tests showed 96.2 tok/s prose decode for Qwen3.8‑27B and 251.7 / 357.9 tok/s for Qwen3.6‑35B‑A3B, while Flash‑Next raised prefill from 45.5 to 65.6 tok/s.
The H200 NVL GPU delivered 229.1 tok/s decode and 17,546 tok/s prefill for DeepSeek‑V4.1‑Flash, though it crashed under load.
perche: Faster local serving reduces latency and hardware costs for anyone running free models such as Kimi K3 or GLM‑5.3.
